the global soil C pool has been declining since the dawn of agriculture, and the rate of soil C loss has accelerated with industrialization, and soil C can act as a significant sink for atmospheric CO2.
the potential for soil C sequestration to mitigate CO2 emissions and to improve global food security is significant.

(i) soil C storage can be increased by improving the efficiency of C cycling through management practices, (ii) C sequestration is not a panacea for climate change, (iii) C sequestratlon in soils can be achieved by using a wide array of management practices, and (iv) the economic potential of C sequestration in soils is high, and the cobenefits are significant, especially in developing nations

soil is the key to global food security.
soils have a significant capacity for C storage, but the potential is not fully realized.
the soil C pool is a dynamic, global C pool that is a major source and sink for atmospheric CO2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the soil C pool is an important and dynamic component of the global C balance and is critical to the global food supply.
soil C sequestration is a win-win-win strategy for the environment, the economy, and society.
soil C is a dynamic and important pool of terrestrial organic matter that is essential to maintaining ecosystem health, productivity, and sustainability and is critical in the global carbon cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the potential of soil C storage as a climate mitigation strategy is large but is currently not fully realized.

we need to develop a global strategy that includes the following components: 1) increase the efficiency of fertilizer N and P use to reduce the loss of these elements from the soil, 2) increase the use of organic amendments and manure to increase the soil C and N pool, 3) increase the use and adoption of cover crops and no-till to increase the C sequestration potential of the soil, and 4) improve the soil quality and fertility through the adoption of conservation practices
soil C sequestration is a critical tool for mitigating climate change and improving soil quality, and thus, global food security.
